description: THE MULTI-ROW ACCUMULATION CASE. Four TCATBALF rows under ONE account (00000000001), which isolates three behaviours no single-row case can reach: (1) ADD WS-MONTHLY-INT TO WS-TOTAL-INT [app/cbl/CBACT04C.cbl:467] accumulates PER ROW over four separately truncated values, reaching exactly 7.47; (2) WS-TRANID-SUFFIX advances once per WRITE, not once per account, giving the contiguous suffixes 000001 through 000004; and (3) the DISCGRP rate lookup runs once per RECORD, not once per account break, so the fallback message pair repeats FOUR times. CONTROL FLOW, read off :188-222. Only :195-205 sit inside the break test IF TRANCAT-ACCT-ID NOT= WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM [:194]; :210-213 sit OUTSIDE it. WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM is PIC X(11) VALUE SPACES [:167], so the break fires on row 1 only and :201 then makes rows 2-4 compare equal. Therefore the ACCTFILE read [:203] and the alternate-key XREFFILE read [:205] happen ONCE, and MOVE 0 TO WS-TOTAL-INT [:200] happens ONCE, while the rate lookup [:213], the interest computation [:215], the write [:468] and the fees no-op [:216] happen FOUR times. (3) IS THE ASSERTION A PLAUSIBLE IMPLEMENTATION FAILS, by hoisting the rate lookup into the break handler where it looks like it belongs. Because :210-213 are outside the break block, the DISCGRP read is re-executed on every record even though the account never changes; an implementation that cached the rate per account would emit the fallback pair ONCE and fail here. Every row misses its group and takes the '23'-then-DEFAULT path [:436-438], so each of the four rows emits 'DISCLOSURE GROUP RECORD MISSING' [:418] then 'TRY WITH DEFAULT GROUP CODE' [:419] - 14 messages in total: START + 4 x (50-byte DISPLAY TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD [:193], MISSING, TRY-DEFAULT) + END. No error line appears: every open, read, write and close succeeds, and status '23' is explicitly not an error at :422. WHY EVERY ROW MISSES - A CORRECTION TO THE FOLDER BRIEF (practice B4). The brief states that account 1 carries group id A000000000. It does not. Read mechanically against CVACT01Y (11+1+12+12+12+10+10+10+12+12+10+10+178 = 300), ACCT-GROUP-ID occupies bytes 113-122 and is TEN SPACES; the literal A000000000 sits at bytes 103-112, which is ACCT-ADDR-ZIP. Stronger still: not one of the 50 rows of acctdata.txt has a non-blank ACCT-GROUP-ID, so every account in this fixture takes the DEFAULT fallback. The key built at :210-212 is a 16-byte DIS-GROUP-KEY per CVTRA02Y, so a blank group id cannot match A000000000 even where the type and category do. NUMERIC PARITY: SCALE 2, RoundingMode.DOWN, TRUNCATED PER ROW. COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200 [:464-465] carries NO ROUNDED phrase - the keyword appears zero times in all 28 programs - and stores into WS-MONTHLY-INT PIC S9(09)V99 [:168], so the faithful Java is setScale(2, RoundingMode.DOWN) through common.CobolDecimal, never HALF_UP and never HALF_EVEN. DIS-INT-RATE is read at PIC S9(04)V99 from bytes 17-22 of the DEFAULT row and is 15.00 for all four seeded keys (verified in discgrp.txt rows 17, 27, 28 and 29). Row by row: 194.00 x 15.00 / 1200 = 2.4250 -> 2.42 (HALF_UP would give 2.43); 158.00 -> 1.9750 -> 1.97 (HALF_UP 1.98, HALF_EVEN 1.98); 147.00 -> 1.8375 -> 1.83 (HALF_UP 1.84, HALF_EVEN 1.84); 100.00 -> 1.2500 -> 1.25 exactly. Rows 1-3 are therefore half-boundary discriminators - all three differ from HALF_UP and two of them also differ from HALF_EVEN - while row 4 is an exact quotient acting as a control. THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS IS ITSELF AN ASSERTION. The program truncates EACH row to scale 2 and only then sums: 2.42 + 1.97 + 1.83 + 1.25 = 7.47. Summing the exact quotients first (2.4250 + 1.9750 + 1.8375 + 1.2500 = 7.4875) and truncating once would give 7.48. That contrast is the strongest available proof that truncation happens per COMPUTE at the receiver's declared scale, exactly as the COBOL does, and not once at the end - so a total of 7.48 anywhere, or an amount of 0000000024C, 0000000019H or 0000000018D, signals a wrong rounding mode or a wrong truncation point. THE SUFFIX ADVANCES PER WRITE, NOT PER ACCOUNT. ADD 1 TO WS-TRANID-SUFFIX [:474] sits inside 1300-B-WRITE-TX, which 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST performs once per record at :468, so four rows under one account yield four contiguous suffixes. Because WS-TRANID-SUFFIX is PIC 9(06) VALUE 0 [:173] and the ADD precedes the STRING at :476-480, the sequence starts at 000001 and never emits 000000. PARM-DATE X(10) followed by WS-TRANID-SUFFIX PIC 9(06) fills TRAN-ID PIC X(16) exactly. IDENTICAL ON ALL FOUR RECORDS, WHICH IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE AND DELIBERATE: TRAN-TYPE-CD is '01' [:482]; TRAN-CAT-CD is '0005' because MOVE '05' [:483] is an unconditional literal move into a numeric-display PIC 9(04) receiver, so the four DIFFERENT input categories (0001, 0001, 0002, 0003) never reach the output and drive only the rate lookup; TRAN-DESC is 'Int. for a/c 00000000001' followed by 76 spaces, because all four rows share one account, the literal at :485 is 13 characters including its trailing space, ACCT-ID adds 11 for 24, and STRING does not blank the receiver tail while common.FixedWidthCodec space-initialises the record; TRAN-CARD-NUM is 9680294154603697, the XREF-CARD-NUM of the only cardxref.txt row whose bytes 26-36 hold 00000000001 (zero-based row 48 - the file is ordered by card number, which is why the program reads it through the ALTERNATE key FD-XREF-ACCT-ID); and both timestamps carry one pinned value, since :496-498 move a single DB2-FORMAT-TS into TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS. Each record is 350 bytes with FILLER X(20) emitted as spaces, matching CVTRA05Y and INTCALC.jcl:39 RECFM=F,LRECL=350. NO ACCTFILE REWRITE, AND THE REASON IS EXACT. All four rows belong to account 1, so there is exactly ONE account break and it is the FIRST: WS-FIRST-TIME is 'Y' at :195, which routes to :198 and merely flips the flag rather than performing 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT. Rows 2-4 cause no break at all. The only other call site, the ELSE at :219-220, is UNREACHABLE DEAD CODE - PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' [:188] guarantees that IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' [:189] is true whenever the loop body runs - so the final, and here only, account group is never rewritten. Practice B5 forbids repairing that. The assertion is meaningful rather than vacuous because ACCTFILE is opened I-O [:291], so a rewrite was genuinely possible: expectedFinalState pins all 50 account rows byte-identical to acctdata.txt, and the whole file contains only two output verbs, REWRITE at :356 and WRITE at :500. The consequence is that WS-TOTAL-INT reaches 7.47 but is never applied to ACCT-CURR-BAL in this run, so the accumulation is proved INDIRECTLY here - by the four TRAN-AMT values summing to 7.47 rather than 7.48 - while case11.json owns the direct observation of WS-TOTAL-INT reaching ACCT-CURR-BAL. 1400-COMPUTE-FEES is invoked four times, because :216 sits inside the satisfied IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0 guard at :214 on every row, but its body is the comment '* To be implemented' followed by EXIT [:518-520], so it contributes no record, no field and no message on any of the four passes. PROVENANCE, STATED HONESTLY (practice B12). Every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED from the COBOL paragraphs, the copybook byte layouts, the JCL DD and PARM contract and the ASCII fixtures. None of it is captured from an execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment (AAP 0.7.6, risk R-A). All FOUR TCATBALF rows are MODIFIED rather than quoted: every one of the 50 real tcatbal.txt balances is 0000000000{ (0.00) and every real row uses key 01/0001, so the fixture can supply neither a non-zero balance nor the three extra category keys. The amounts are nevertheless fixture-derived - 194.00, 158.00, 147.00 and 100.00 are the real ACCT-CURR-BAL values of accounts 1, 2, 3 and 49 in acctdata.txt - and 04/0001 through 04/0003 are real keys present in every discgrp.txt block. The 22-byte FILLER span keeps the zero fill the real fixture uses. ACCTFILE, XREFFILE, XREFFIL1 and DISCGRP are seeded from the unmodified fixtures; XREFFILE and XREFFIL1 are two access paths over ONE base KSDS (INTCALC.jcl:29 and :31, gate G45) and cardxref.txt is left at its literal 36 bytes, with the 36-to-50 pad declared as a normalisation so it is applied once at seed time rather than baked into the case (gate G16). THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE FOLDER BRIEF'S SPELLING, recorded rather than applied silently (B4). First, the brief asks for a member named 'expectedRecords'; ParityCase declares no such member and binds strictly, so the ordered writes are carried in expectedWrites and the untouched post-state in expectedFinalState, which is the split the model documents. Second, the brief pins the timestamp to 2022-07-18-00.00.00.000000; the harness owns that value and ParityHarness.DEFAULT_PINNED_CLOCK is 2022-07-19T23:12:34, which Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP [:613-626] renders as the 26-byte 2022-07-19-23.12.34.000000, so that is what is pinned - fixed and never a captured now (practice B7). Third, the brief calls the output TRANSACT, which is the JCL DD name; application.yml resolves that DD to the SYSTRAN entry for this job, so the writes are addressed by the binding key SYSTRAN. No dataset is addressed by a literal dataset name anywhere (gate G46). None of the three alters the substance of the case. GATES: G28 is the headline - four executions of the COMPUTE at :464-465 and four of the ADD at :467 - with G23, G24 and G25 on the truncation, G15, G17 and G18 on the field-by-field diff, G19, G20 and G21 on the four 350-byte records and their FILLER, G26 on the fees no-op, G45, G16, G46 and G51, the unit being reached as a batch job with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path.
